newsitem.title: INDIA: India's oil pool deficit seen at $5.0 billion.
newsitem.headline: India's oil pool deficit seen at $5.0 billion.

text.p: India's oil pool deficit is expected to soar to 184 billion rupees ($5.14 billion) at the end of March from previous estimates of 155 billion, the Economic Times newspaper said on Friday.
The newspaper quoted Petroleum Ministry estimates as saying the deficit would touch this level if world crude prices continue at the current level of about $22 per barrel.
Petroleum Ministry officials have said domestic oil product prices must be raised to curtail the burgeoning cost of an oil subsidy programme.

Earlier estimates had said the deficit, which is the amount the government owes Indian oil companies for selling petroleum products to Indian consumers below world prices, would reach 155 billion rupees by March 31, the end of fiscal 1996/97.
"Sources said the government would have no other option but to increase prices and resort to government borrowings to meet the deficit," the Economic Times said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, bowing to pressures from coalition partners, last week ruled out a hike in petroleum product prices in the near future, and said the government would wait for a consensus to emerge on the issue.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's communist partners in the 13-party centre-left coalition and the right-wing opposition Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have urged him to resist calls to raise oil prices.
Deve Gowda said last month the government might resort to borrowing to plug the deficit on the oil pool account. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
